newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks, peso seen nervous on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks, peso seen nervous on Brazil.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen down on Brazil jitters
--Cetes overnight rate viewed up on weak peso

Traders saw Mexican markets being rattled across the board on Friday from another round of the "samba effect" triggered by an early sharp fall in Brazilian equities. The Bovespa index in Sao Paulo plunged 3.47 percent to 11,322 points at the open.
"We withstood the fall in Brazil yesterday, but this is too much to ignore, dealers are bound to be nervous," a desk trader said.
Technical analysts saw support at 4,790 points on Mexico's IPC index, down from Thursday's close of 4,816.37.
Traders expected the peso to open under great pressure due to fallout from a sell-off on Brazilian equities markets.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8900/7.9400 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9175/7.9250 per dollar, sharply weaker than Thursday's close of 7.8530/7.8580.
Overnight Cetes rates were seen opening sharply up under pressure from forecast weakness in the foreign exchange market.((--Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
